physical.title: cloth
physical.summary: Kente cloth, a rectangular woman’s wrapper composed of 11 hand-woven narrow strips of imported European cotton and rayon, hand-sewn together along the selvedges. The strips are designed and assembled to form a chequerboard pattern; both ends have a variant design of five bands of weft blocks that serve as a border to the main field. All the strips have a uniform ground design with lines of blue, red, green, yellow, white and black cotton in the warp; the ground weft is blue cotton, and the supplementary designs are in red and yellow rayon. The weft pattern consists of supplementary discontinuous designs between bands of continuous thread. The warp ends have been left as a fringe.
